proposals.before: He loved low carts and ponies, ordering attendants to gallop them, cutting cheek-straps and cheek-pieces so riders fell for sport.
proposals.after: He loved low carts and ponies; he had attendants gallop them, then cut their harness straps and bridles to amuse himself by making them fall.
proposals.reason: The literal also mistranslates the harness straps and bridles as cheek-straps and cheek-pieces.

proposals.before: Plots of slaughtered victims were already woven; dog-burial slanders proceeded apace.
proposals.after: The plot involving a sacrificial victim had already been laid; the slander involving a dead dog then took effect.
proposals.reason: The literal adds burial to the dead-dog slander, although bi-quan only states the dead/killed dog. Retain both source images without inventing allusion participants.
